title: [Debatable] Stale concurrent session can silently overwrite newly saved orders
body:
## Problem

Two independent application sessions sharing the same data file can silently overwrite each other's successful changes. A read-only command in the older session can remove an order already saved by the newer session.

## Environment and verification

- Windows, Java 25.0.4.
- Reproduced against the published `BakeBase-v1.4.jar` and a local packaged build of commit `c7d1930a2bd002cb1c24f0864a06b35c93182a9c`.
- Verified using two independent `ModelManager`/`LogicManager` sessions loaded from the same JSON file, exercising the packaged code and real storage writes. Two full GUI processes have not yet been used to confirm this reproduction.

## Verified reproduction

1. Save a populated book containing 24 orders.
2. Load that saved book into independent sessions A and B, both pointing to the same file.
3. In A, execute `add-order 1 i/1 q/123 d/2026-12-01`.
4. Read the saved file: it contains 25 orders.
5. In the older B, execute `list-orders`.
6. Read the saved file again: it contains 24 orders. A's newly saved order has disappeared, without a stale-data warning.

For manual confirmation, launch two BakeBase processes from the same disposable home folder before step 3, issue the commands in their respective windows, then reopen the saved book.

## Expected behavior

An older session must not silently overwrite changes saved by another session. Either prevent simultaneous use of the same data folder or detect the stale file and reject the overwrite with a clear recovery message.

## Cause and suggested direction

[`LogicManager.execute`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/c7d1930a2bd002cb1c24f0864a06b35c93182a9c/src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/LogicManager.java#L83-L84) saves its entire in-memory book after every successful command, including listing. There is no stale-version check or session lock protecting the shared book. The unconditional-save behavior is inherited from AB3.

Consider an OS-managed exclusive lock for the data folder, or optimistic version checking before saving. Skipping writes for read-only commands narrows this trigger but does not protect against the older session's next data change or undo.

## Priority and triage

**Priority: Medium.** Silent loss of successfully saved records warrants investigation, although simultaneous sessions may be uncommon. PE acceptance and severity remain conditional on whether concurrent use is considered in scope. This report does not claim a failure of normal single-session order operations.
display_title: [Debatable] Stale concurrent session can silently overwrite newly saved orders

title: Default client cards truncate delivery addresses without an expand or tooltip option
body:
**Environment:** Windows, Java 25.0.4.1. Verified against the published v1.4 JAR and unchanged production sources compiled from commit `1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2` using the release dependencies.

## Steps

1. Launch in a fresh disposable folder with no saved preferences, using the default window size.
2. Inspect the first sample client, Alex Yeoh.
3. Compare the visible address with the actual sample address: `Blk 30 Geylang Street 29, #06-40`.

## Actual

The client card truncates the address with an ellipsis, hiding the complete unit number. Other sample addresses are also cut off. There is no address tooltip, text wrapping, or expandable detail view on the card.

Observed in the native v1.4 GUI. A rendered 205-logical-pixel-wide actual `PersonCard`, representing the client-card space in the default three-column layout, reports:

```text
ADDRESS_STORED=Blk 30 Geylang Street 29, #06-40
ADDRESS_RENDERED=Blk 30 Geylang Street 29, #06-...
ADDRESS_WRAPS=false
ADDRESS_TOOLTIP=null
```

The same output is reproduced with the current source. The precise truncation point depends on fonts, scale and available width.

## Expected

The baker should be able to read the complete delivery address through the client UI, using wrapping, a tooltip, copying, or an expandable details view. The app's own ordinary sample addresses should remain accessible in its default window.

## Impact and scope

The saved address remains intact. Enlarging the window is a workaround; this is not data loss. A no-op client edit can also expose the full address in feedback, but that is an indirect workaround for viewing an existing record.

[PersonListCard.fxml, line 32](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2/src/main/resources/view/PersonListCard.fxml#L32) uses a single-line label. `PersonCard` supplies the full text without a tooltip. This differs from the order labels, which already wrap.

This is separate from #110's screen/minimum-height constraint: the problem occurs within the default window with ordinary sample data, even when the whole window fits the display.
display_title: Default client cards truncate delivery addresses without an expand or tooltip option

title: Item and order searches miss natural words next to parentheses
body:
**Environment:** Windows, Java 25.0.4.1. Verified against the published v1.4 JAR and unchanged production sources compiled from commit `1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2` using the release dependencies.

## Steps

Use a fresh disposable book and run:

```text
add-client n/Alice p/12345678 e/alice@example.com a/One Road
add-item n/Chocolate (Gluten Free) p/5
add-order 1 i/1 q/2 d/2026-12-01
find-items Free
find-orders Free
```

## Actual

Both searches report zero results, even though the item and its order exist and the name contains the natural word `Free`.

Controls:

```text
find-items Free)
find-orders Free)
```

Each returns one result. Likewise, `find-items (Gluten` finds the item, whereas the unpunctuated word does not match. Verified through actual parser, commands, model and real storage in both the published v1.4 JAR and current source.

## Expected improvement

Natural words adjacent to ordinary parentheses should be searchable without requiring users to remember the punctuation. Bakery names commonly include parenthesized dietary information and variants. The UG describes matching whole words; it does not explain that surrounding punctuation becomes part of a search token.

## Cause and triage

[StringUtil.containsWordIgnoreCase, lines 30–38](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2/src/main/java/seedu/address/commons/util/StringUtil.java#L30-L38) splits names only on whitespace and compares complete tokens. Thus `Free)` is a token and `Free` is not.

This is a feature-improvement suggestion. If whitespace-only token matching is intentional, document that limitation clearly in the UG; otherwise, consider supporting natural-word boundaries beside parentheses.

Both commands share the same underlying word-matching rule. This is separate from #134's rejection of punctuation in client names; this example uses an accepted bakery-item name.
display_title: Item and order searches miss natural words next to parentheses

title: Address validation accepts an entirely blank Unicode-whitespace address
body:
**Target milestone:** v1.5 (release candidate).

**Verification:** Windows, Java 25.0.4.1. Tested using the published v1.4 JAR and unchanged production sources compiled from team commit `1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2`, with release dependencies. The documentation findings refer to the current guides at that commit. The v1.5 GitHub release is still a draft; these reports do not claim testing an officially published v1.5 JAR.

## Reproduction

In a disposable book, copy and submit the following command. The character after the final `a/` is **one U+2003 EM SPACE**, not an ordinary ASCII space:

```text
add-client n/Blank Address p/12345678 e/blank@example.com a/ 
```

The same case is accepted through `edit-client INDEX a/` followed by that EM SPACE.

## Actual

The command reports success, saves the client, and leaves a visually blank address. The address also loads successfully after reading the saved book.

The audit submitted the input through the real JavaFX `CommandBox`, including its action handler, and obtained these results in both versions:

```text
TEXTFIELD_PRESERVES_EM_SPACE=true
PERSON_COUNT=1
ADDRESS_LENGTH=1
ADDRESS_CODEPOINT=2003
ADDRESS_IS_BLANK=true
INPUT_CLEARED=true
RELOADED_ADDRESS_IS_BLANK=true
```

## Expected

Reject an address made entirely of whitespace, consistently with the displayed constraint: `Addresses can take any values, and should not be blank`. An invisible Unicode space should not bypass the required-address check.

## Cause and scope

[Address.java, lines 12–18](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2/src/main/java/seedu/address/model/person/Address.java#L12-L18) uses `[^\s].*`. Java's default regex whitespace class does not cover this character, and parser `trim()` also leaves it intact. Java's `String.isBlank()` identifies the stored value as blank.

Apply a consistent nonblank check to add/edit commands and loading saved records. This is a required-field validation issue involving an invisible blank value, rather than a request to support names in additional languages. The inherited AB3 implementation is involved.
display_title: Address validation accepts an entirely blank Unicode-whitespace address

title: Data-file locks prevent typed exit, help, and read-only searches
body:
**Target milestone:** v1.5 (release candidate).

**Verification:** Windows, Java 25.0.4.1. Tested using the published v1.4 JAR and unchanged production sources compiled from team commit `1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2`, with release dependencies. The documentation findings refer to the current guides at that commit. The v1.5 GitHub release is still a draft; these reports do not claim testing an officially published v1.5 JAR.

## Reproduction

1. Launch in a disposable folder and run `populate`, allowing it to save successfully.
2. Keep `data/addressbook.json` readable but hold a file handle that denies deletion/replacement. For example, in a separate PowerShell session in that disposable folder:

```powershell
$alphaLock = [System.IO.File]::Open(
    (Resolve-Path './data/addressbook.json').Path,
    [System.IO.FileMode]::Open,
    [System.IO.FileAccess]::Read,
    [System.IO.FileShare]::ReadWrite)
```

3. In the app, submit `exit`, then `help`, then `find-items Muffin`.
4. Use the Help menu while the same handle is still open.
5. Release the handle with `$alphaLock.Dispose()` and retry the commands.

## Actual

All three typed commands fail with a save/permissions error. `exit` leaves the main window open, typed `help` does not open Help, and the search is rolled back. The Help menu still opens Help under the same lock. Once released, the same typed commands succeed.

The actual `MainWindow` command-input action handler produced these flags in both tested versions:

```text
LOCKED_EXIT_MAIN_STILL_SHOWING=true
LOCKED_EXIT_REPORTED_SAVE_ERROR=true
LOCKED_HELP_SHOWING=false
MENU_HELP_DURING_LOCK_SHOWING=true
DATA_UNCHANGED=true
UNLOCKED_EXIT_MAIN_STILL_SHOWING=false
```

The existing book had already saved successfully, and the tests confirmed its contents were unchanged. This is not a failed data-edit operation or an attempt to launch in a write-protected directory.

## Expected

Commands that do not change bakery-book data should remain usable when the saved file is temporarily unavailable for replacement. In particular, typed Help and Exit should provide the same basic functionality as the menu actions. Failed data changes must retain the existing rollback protections.

## Cause and scope

[LogicManager.execute, lines 81–84](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2/src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/LogicManager.java#L81-L84) saves after every successful command. A save failure throws before [MainWindow handles the Help/Exit result](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/MainWindow.java#L197-L206).

This is a rare failure-handling issue with menu workarounds. It shares the inherited unconditional-save path implicated by #130, but has a different trigger and effect: no second application session or silent overwrite is involved. Group Help, Exit and searches into this single report.
display_title: Data-file locks prevent typed exit, help, and read-only searches

title: Clarify the unimplemented deadline-cutoff filtering use case in the DG
body:
**Target milestone:** v1.5 (release candidate).

**Verification:** Windows, Java 25.0.4.1. Tested using the published v1.4 JAR and unchanged production sources compiled from team commit `1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2`, with release dependencies. The documentation findings refer to the current guides at that commit. The v1.5 GitHub release is still a draft; these reports do not claim testing an officially published v1.5 JAR.

## Documentation

The [DG use case “Display unfulfilled orders with deadline soon”](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2/docs/DeveloperGuide.md#L486-L501) describes:

- The user requests incomplete orders with a deadline on/before a specified date.
- The system displays matching orders, or says none are due on/before that date.

It appears among the ordinary use cases and is not marked proposed or unimplemented.

## Actual implemented behavior

`list-incomplete-orders` filters only by completion status. Its sole optional argument, `by-deadline`, sorts earliest first; it does not hide orders beyond a cutoff. `find-orders` searches client/item names, rather than dates. The full command dispatch exposes no dedicated date-cutoff command.

For example, both attempted date arguments are rejected:

```text
list-incomplete-orders 2026-11-01
list-incomplete-orders by-deadline d/2026-11-01
```

The error lists only `Parameters: [by-deadline]`. The DG itself supplies no alternate command syntax for performing its described date-cutoff workflow.

## Requested clarification

If this is planned work, label the use case as proposed/unimplemented. If it is meant to document the delivered release, revise it to describe the available completion filter and deadline sorting, or identify the implemented command that supplies the stated behavior.

This report requests accurate documentation rather than treating an arbitrary guessed command spelling as a required API or asking the team to add a new feature during a freeze. A use case may intentionally describe future scope, so that interpretation should be clarified before treating this as a confirmed implementation defect.

Relevant implementation: [ListIncompleteOrdersCommand](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2/src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/commands/ListIncompleteOrdersCommand.java), [AddressBookParser](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/1508e3794536988a0fef612fc90a4e9643adfab2/src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/parser/AddressBookParser.java).
display_title: Clarify the unimplemented deadline-cutoff filtering use case in the DG

title: [Debatable] Clients without an email address cannot be recorded
body:
# BH-0001: Clients without an email address cannot be recorded

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | type.FeatureFlaw |
| Severity | severity.Medium |
| Investigation state | confirmed |
| Confidence | high in observed behavior/text; grading acceptance remains a separate judgment |
| Grading component | Product design |
| Affected feature/document | add-client / required email |
| Artifact/revision | Current source e449792e137b14dcb3017da2c688d2a71f677a25; clean tracked tree. No release-JAR claim. |
| Environment | Windows; Oracle Java 25.0.4; Gradle 9.6.1; JavaFX 17.0.7. Published docs inspected in the in-app browser on 2026-10-30. |
| First seen | 2026-10-30 |
| Updated | 2026-10-30 |
| Last checked | 2026-10-30 |
| Rule verification | Live PE, grading and relevant constraints read 2026-10-30; not snapshot-only. |
| Developer response | not recorded |
| Assignee(s) | unknown |
| Relationship | related; canonical independent finding |

## Summary

A home baker taking a phone or messaging order cannot register a customer who has no email address, even when their phone and delivery address are known.

## Preconditions and reproduction

Start with an empty disposable bakery book (`clear confirm`).

1. Enter `add-client n/Carol p/93456789 a/30 Test Road`.
2. Try an explicit empty email: `add-client n/Carol p/93456789 e/ a/30 Test Road`.
3. Try to create an order for Carol.

All application inputs use disposable data. To replay the retained probe, run the command in the [audit index](README.md); do not run destructive setup against a real bakery book.

## Expected result

A usable customer record should be possible with a name, working phone number, and address. Email should not be compulsory for a phone-order workflow.

Basis: [product documentation](../../docs/UserGuide.md#adding-a-client-add-client) and the home-baker target profile in [DG Product scope](../../docs/DeveloperGuide.md#product-scope).

## Actual result and evidence

The first command is rejected as invalid format; blank email values fail email validation. No client is created, preventing its orders from being recorded. The isolated missing-email command and the blank-field rejection were executed.

[Executed command transcript](evidence/2026-10-30-probe.txt).

## Impact and classification

- **Type rationale:** The delivered design obstructs the concrete home-baker workflow above. Its documented behavior is not being misclassified as a parser/specification mismatch.
- **Severity rationale:** Bakers occasionally receive customers' orders without email details. They must invent an email, obtain unnecessary information, or record the order elsewhere. Other customers remain usable.
- **Scope assessment:** Current-source beta audit, assessed using the live AY2026/27 S1 rubric. Final PE release applicability must be rechecked on its supplied binary/documents. Documented limitations are considered in severity and scope; confirmation of the behavior does not constitute official acceptance.
- **Acceptance uncertainty:** This is documented behavior, not a parser mismatch. A scope defense is possible; the concern is that the mandatory field obstructs an ordinary phone-order workflow.

## Verification and cause

Verified: `AddCommandParser#parse` requires PREFIX_EMAIL, and `ParserUtil#parseEmail` rejects empty values.

The existing suite passed 579 tests with zero failures, errors, or skips. This does not establish released-binary coverage. Detailed experiment boundaries are in [README](README.md).
display_title: [Debatable] Clients without an email address cannot be recorded

title: Refresh the UG Help screenshot to show clear confirmation and undo
body:

title: Qualify the UG claim that marked orders remain visible under completion filters
body:
Verified during beta testing of the published v1.5 JAR on Windows with Java 25.0.4, against the release guides at commit `e449792e137b14dcb3017da2c688d2a71f677a25`. Suggested PE classification: `type.DocumentationBug`, `severity.Low`.

## Problem

The [mark-order-complete section](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/UserGuide.md#L308) unconditionally states that the order remains visible in the order panel. The [completion-filter section](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/UserGuide.md#L383-L384) correctly says marking removes it from the incomplete view.

## Reproduction

In a disposable empty book:

```text
add-client n/Alpha Baker p/12345678 e/alpha@example.com a/Home
add-item n/Seasonal Tart p/10
add-order 1 i/1 q/1 d/2026-11-03
list-incomplete-orders
mark 1 o/1
list-orders
```

After marking, the stored order count remains one but the incomplete view contains zero orders. `list-orders` shows the completed order again. Filtering works correctly; the unconditional visibility promise can make users think an order unexpectedly disappeared.

## Fix and acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replace the unconditional statement with wording such as: “Marking an order does not delete it. It remains visible in the all-orders view, but disappears from the incomplete-orders view. Use list-orders to show all orders again.”
- [ ] Keep the marking and completion-filter sections consistent.
- [ ] Replay the sequence and verify the rendered UG describes both views accurately.

No change to completion-filter behavior is required.
display_title: Qualify the UG claim that marked orders remain visible under completion filters

title: Replace the DG storage-testing placeholder with executable recovery tests
body:
Verified during beta testing of the published v1.5 JAR on Windows with Java 25.0.4, against the release guides at commit `e449792e137b14dcb3017da2c688d2a71f677a25`. Suggested PE classification: `type.DocumentationBug`, `severity.Low`.

## Problem

The [DG data-storage manual-testing subsection](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/DeveloperGuide.md#L622-L628) still contains an authoring placeholder asking the team to explain missing/corrupted-file simulation and expected behavior. It does not provide usable test steps.

This prevents a tester from following the advertised storage-recovery checks and leaves overwrite consequences unexplained.

## Fix and acceptance criteria

Use a disposable writable folder and keep a separate valid backup. Document these cases:

- [ ] **Missing file:** close the app, move `data/addressbook.json` elsewhere, and relaunch. Expect sample data.
- [ ] **Invalid JSON:** close the app, replace the test file contents with an incomplete JSON object such as `{"persons":`, and relaunch. Expect an empty book without a startup crash.
- [ ] **Subsequent save:** run a successful saving command such as `list-clients`. Expect the current fallback book to be written to disk, replacing the missing/invalid file.
- [ ] **Recovery:** close the app, restore a valid backup, and relaunch. Expect its records and associations.
- [ ] Explicitly warn that saving after fallback can overwrite the invalid file; retain backups outside the tested path.
- [ ] Remove the authoring placeholders and execute the documented procedure before publishing.

This is incomplete testing documentation, not a claim that storage recovery itself fails.
display_title: Replace the DG storage-testing placeholder with executable recovery tests

title: A syntactically valid apostrophe email cannot be stored
body:
# BH-0008: A syntactically valid apostrophe email cannot be stored

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |

| Severity | severity.Low |
| Investigation state | confirmed |
| Confidence | high in observed behavior/text; grading acceptance remains a separate judgment |

| Environment | Windows; Oracle Java 25.0.4; Gradle 9.6.1; JavaFX 17.0.7. Published docs inspected in the in-app browser on 2026-10-30. |

| Developer response | not recorded |
| Assignee(s) | unknown |
| Relationship | related; canonical independent finding |

## Summary

The email validator rejects an ordinary apostrophe in the local part, although that spelling is allowed by email syntax.

## Preconditions and reproduction

Enter `add-client n/O'Neil p/93456789 e/o'neil@example.com a/30 Test Road` in a disposable book.

All application inputs use disposable data. To replay the retained probe, run the command in the [audit index](README.md); do not run destructive setup against a real bakery book.

## Expected result

A contact manager should retain the customer's valid email spelling. RFC 5322 sections 3.2.3 and 3.4.1 allow apostrophe in an unquoted dot-atom local part.

Basis: [product documentation](../../docs/UserGuide.md#adding-a-client-add-client) and the home-baker target profile in [DG Product scope](../../docs/DeveloperGuide.md#product-scope).

## Actual result and evidence

The email-constraint error rejects the record. Removing the apostrophe would change the mailbox rather than merely normalize formatting. No claim is made that the illustrative mailbox actually exists.

[Executed command transcript](evidence/2026-10-30-probe.txt).

## Impact and classification

- **Type rationale:** The delivered design obstructs the concrete home-baker workflow above. Its documented behavior is not being misclassified as a parser/specification mismatch.
- **Severity rationale:** A small subset of customers cannot have their correct email recorded. Another email or an external note is required; conservative Low reflects the uncommon spelling.
- **Scope assessment:** Current-source beta audit, assessed using the live AY2026/27 S1 rubric. Final PE release applicability must be rechecked on its supplied binary/documents. Documented limitations are considered in severity and scope; confirmation of the behavior does not constitute official acceptance.
- **Acceptance uncertainty:** The product does not promise full RFC support and provides a precise error. The restriction is still a potential over-validation flaw; grading acceptance is not assumed.

## Verification and cause

Verified: `Email.SPECIAL_CHARACTERS` permits only `+_.-`; its regular expression excludes apostrophe.

The existing suite passed 579 tests with zero failures, errors, or skips. This does not establish released-binary coverage. Detailed experiment boundaries are in [README](README.md).

## Summary

The glossary's order definition implies optional deadline/status fields despite mandatory domain invariants.

## Preconditions and reproduction

Read the Client order entry in DG Glossary (line 528). Compare with UG's required `d/DEADLINE`, the ClientOrder constructor, and JSON loader validation.

All application inputs use disposable data. To replay the retained probe, run the command in the [audit index](README.md); do not run destructive setup against a real bakery book.

## Expected result

The definition should reflect that every order has a deadline and completion status; a new order starts incomplete.

Basis: [product documentation](../../docs/DeveloperGuide.md#glossary) and the home-baker target profile in [DG Product scope](../../docs/DeveloperGuide.md#product-scope).

## Actual result and evidence

The entry qualifies deadline and status with `if specified`. `ClientOrder` requires non-null Deadline and primitive boolean status; storage rejects missing deadline or complete.

[Document inspection notes](evidence/2026-10-30-document-inspection.md).

## Impact and classification

- **Type rationale:** The problem is in the guide's accuracy, completeness, or wording; the report does not request changing appropriate application behavior.
- **Severity rationale:** A developer can incorrectly design optional fields or fixtures that the model refuses. Detailed implementation sections clarify the invariant, limiting the disruption.
- **Scope assessment:** Current-source beta audit, assessed using the live AY2026/27 S1 rubric. Final PE release applicability must be rechecked on its supplied binary/documents. 
- **Acceptance uncertainty:** No official developer response exists. The stated evidence supports a local finding; final triage remains the team's/course's decision.

## Verification and cause

Confirmed by rendered glossary and model/storage inspection. This is a documentation invariant mismatch, not an attempt to allow missing fields in JSON.

The existing suite passed 579 tests with zero failures, errors, or skips. This does not establish released-binary coverage. Detailed experiment boundaries are in [README](README.md).
